name: Can damaged doors, trim, and cabinetry in a foreclosed home be repaired instead of replaced?

mainEntity.name: Can damaged doors, trim, and cabinetry in a foreclosed home be repaired instead of replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: Reputable remodeling contractors evaluate whether doors, cabinets, and millwork can be salvaged through skilled carpentry and repainting or require outright replacement. Solid wood doors, salvageable cabinet boxes, and intact baseboards can frequently be planed, patched, and painted to save on renovation costs. However, swelling particleboard, warped cabinet frames, and water-softened jambs must be replaced to ensure long-term durability. A finish carpenter can determine which interior elements retain structural integrity and which will cost more in labor to patch than to replace with fresh materials.
acceptedAnswer.description: Solid wood and sound cabinets can often be planed, patched, and painted, but swollen particleboard and warped door jambs should be replaced.
